title: lore sync has no fail-closed option when log regeneration would drop unrecognized content
description:
`lore sync` regenerates `docs/log.md` as a MERGE (LCLI-485): committed entries the visible git
history can no longer account for are carried forward, and every line that is neither structure nor
a legible entry is counted into `LogMergeStats.dropped` and reported as a warning. That warning is
deliberately emitted before the write and on `--dry-run` too. It is the right behaviour for an
operator watching a terminal.

IT IS THE WRONG BEHAVIOUR FOR AN UNATTENDED RUN, which is the request. A warning is a signal that
requires a reader. A CI job, a scheduled sync, or an agent loop has none: the run exits 0, the drop
is real, and the loss is discovered later in a diff someone thinks to take. Wanted: an OPT-IN option
that makes `lore sync` REFUSE BEFORE ANY WRITES when regeneration would drop unrecognized log
content. Default behaviour (warn, proceed, exit 0) must not change -- this is fail-closed as a
choice, not a new default.

PROVENANCE: downstream validation feedback on the published lore 0.6.2 / quest 0.6.2 pair, from host
mbpm2, which runs a real integration consumer against the published CLIs. 2026-09-14. Their 0.6.2
run PASSED -- 99 repository workflow tests, zero skips, and lore's history preservation, drop
warnings, accounting, dry-run and `--no-index` behaviour all passed. They flagged this EXPLICITLY as
a feature suggestion, not a failed fix and not a regression. Evidence at
`results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-quest-0.6.2-20260914/validation-report.md`
on mbpm2; ask them rather than guessing at their setup if more detail is needed.

WHERE THE CODE IS, verified 2026-09-14 on dev at 661529cf, not inferred:

- `src/core/log.ts` -- `generateLogWithStats` / `LogMergeStats`. `dropped` is the count,
  `droppedSamples` is up to DROPPED_SAMPLE_LIMIT (3) of the lines verbatim, bounded on purpose.
- `src/commands/sync.ts:241` -- `if (regenerated !== undefined && regenerated.log.dropped > 0)`
  builds `droppedContentWarning` and flushes it.

THE CHECK POINT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY IN THE RIGHT PLACE, which is what makes this small.
`regenerateIndexAndLog` STAGES into the `writes` map; it does not write. The whole write phase --
the symlink preflight, `writeManyAtomicOrRollback`, and `sweepTrackerStorage` -- is gated behind the
`if (!parsed.dryRun)` blocks that FOLLOW the warning at line 241. So a refusal thrown where the
warning is built is structurally before every docs write and before the tracker sweep.

"BEFORE ANY WRITES" IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST BE PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. A guard that aborts halfway has
already done damage. The one thing I did NOT verify is whether `gatherReconciliation`'s Backlog
round-trip can itself mutate anything before line 241 is reached. Establish that rather than
reasoning from the function's name.

SURFACE IS AN OPEN DECISION, and both arms are defensible: a flag (`--fail-on-drop`, explicit at the
call site, trivially greppable in a CI file) or a `.lore/config.toml` setting (applies to every sync
in a repository without every caller remembering, which is closer to what an unattended workflow
actually wants). Doing both is legitimate. Whoever takes it should decide and say why.

INTERACTIONS TO SETTLE: `--no-index` skips regeneration entirely (`regenerated` is undefined), so
there is nothing to refuse -- decide whether combining it with the guard is a silent no-op or a
usage error. `--dry-run` already writes nothing, so the guard there is purely about the exit code,
and a nonzero exit from a dry run is arguably exactly what an unattended pre-check wants.

WIDER POINT, recorded because it is why this is worth more than its size: we have spent a great deal
of effort this month on gates that reported and passed. This is a user asking for the fail-closed
variant of exactly that, and they are right to want it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An opt-in option makes `lore sync` exit nonzero and write NOTHING when log regeneration would drop unrecognized lines. Default behaviour -- warn, proceed, exit 0 -- is unchanged, and a test proves the default still passes.

The refusal is proven to happen before ANY write by a test that asserts the on-disk bytes of docs/ AND the tracker storage are byte-identical to before the run -- not merely that the exit code was nonzero. `gatherReconciliation`'s pre-warning Backlog round-trip is established to be non-mutating rather than assumed to be.

The refusal message names what would be dropped -- the count and the bounded `droppedSamples` the existing warning already carries -- so an unattended runner's captured log is enough to act on without re-running interactively.
The exit code is an existing documented `LoreError` type already in sync's manifest `exitCodes`, not a new bare number, and the manifest entry for sync describes the new surface.

The `--no-index` and `--dry-run` interactions are decided, documented and tested: `--no-index` performs no regeneration so there is nothing to refuse, and `--dry-run` writes nothing so the guard there is purely an exit code.
The chosen surface -- flag, `.lore/config.toml` setting, or both -- is recorded WITH ITS REASON, and appears in both `lore sync --help` and `lore manifest --json`.
`bun run lint`, `typecheck` and the test suite pass, and `lore check` exits 0.
